title: A right, but not an obligation

cues.text: Here is a way of holding the idea that makes it easy to carry around. Forget factories for two minutes.
Somebody gives Nell a voucher. It says: you may buy this bicycle for forty pounds, on any day you like. It never expires. And it never forces you to buy anything.
Question. Is the voucher worth anything before she uses it?
Of course it is. Somebody would buy it off her. It gives her a right she would not otherwise have, and it never obliges her to do anything at all.
And here is the point. The moment she uses it, the voucher is gone. She has a bicycle instead. She cannot use it again, and she cannot sell it on.
Now map it across, one line at a time.
The voucher is the chance to build.
Two words for two different values. Intrinsic value is what she would get by using the chance right now.
And the holding premium — some people call it time value — is what the waiting itself is worth.
And that gives the rule, in one line. Use the chance when the holding premium has fallen to zero. Not before.
Before that point, waiting is still worth something, and building throws it away for nothing.
